Hokkaido :: Geography :: Geologic activity :: chunk_0012
See also: [Category:Volcanoes of Hokkaido](/wiki/Category:Volcanoes_of_Hokkaido "Category:Volcanoes of Hokkaido")

Like many areas of Japan, Hokkaido is [seismically](/wiki/Seismology "Seismology") active. Aside from numerous [earthquakes](/wiki/Earthquake "Earthquake"), the following volcanoes are considered still active (at least one eruption since 1850):

* [Hokkaido Koma-ga-take](/wiki/Hokkaido_Koma-ga-take "Hokkaido Koma-ga-take")
* [Mount Meakan](/wiki/Mount_Meakan "Mount Meakan")
* [Mount Tarumae](/wiki/Mount_Tarumae "Mount Tarumae")
* [Mount Tokachi](/wiki/Mount_Tokachi_(Daisetsuzan) "Mount Tokachi (Daisetsuzan)")
* [Mount Usu](/wiki/Mount_Usu "Mount Usu") and [Shōwa-shinzan](/wiki/Sh%C5%8Dwa-shinzan "Shōwa-shinzan")

In [1993, an earthquake](/wiki/1993_Okushiri_earthquake "1993 Okushiri earthquake") of [magnitude 7.7](/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale "Moment magnitude scale") generated a [tsunami](/wiki/Tsunami "Tsunami") which devastated [Okushiri](/wiki/Okushiri,_Hokkaido "Okushiri, Hokkaido"), killing 202 inhabitants. An [earthquake of magnitude 8.3](/wiki/2003_Tokachi_earthquake "2003 Tokachi earthquake") struck near the island on September 26, 2003. On September 6, 2018, an [earthquake of magnitude 6.6](/wiki/2018_Hokkaido_Eastern_Iburi_earthquake "2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi earthquake") struck with its epicenter near the city of [Tomakomai](/wiki/Tomakomai "Tomakomai"), causing a blackout across the whole island.[[58]](#cite_note-USGS-59) On May 16, 2021, an earthquake measuring 6.1 on the Richter scale struck off the coast of Hokkaido.[[59]](#cite_note-60)

fanoutqa_017948.x:
Wright brothers :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
The brothers gained the mechanical skills essential to their success by working for years in their [Dayton, Ohio](/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio")-based shop with printing presses, bicycles, motors, and other machinery. Their work with bicycles, in particular, influenced their belief that an unstable vehicle such as a flying machine could be controlled and balanced with practice.[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrouch2003169-14) This was a trend, as many other aviation pioneers were also dedicated cyclists and involved in the bicycle business in various ways.[[15]](#cite_note-15) From 1900 until their first powered flights in late 1903, the brothers conducted extensive [glider tests](/wiki/Glider_(aircraft)#19th_century "Glider (aircraft)") that also developed their skills as pilots. Their shop mechanic [Charles Taylor](/wiki/Charlie_Taylor_(mechanic) "Charlie Taylor (mechanic)") became an important part of the team, building their first airplane engine in close collaboration with the brothers.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

The Wright brothers' status as inventors of the airplane has been subject to numerous counter-claims. Much controversy persists over the many [competing claims of early aviators](/wiki/Claims_to_the_first_powered_flight "Claims to the first powered flight"). Edward Roach, historian for the [Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park](/wiki/Dayton_Aviation_Heritage_National_Historical_Park "Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park"), argues that the Wrights were excellent self-taught engineers who could run a small company well, but did not have the business skills or temperament necessary to dominate the rapidly growing aviation industry at the time.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

Lionel Messi :: Philanthropy :: part 01 :: chunk_0028
Throughout his career, Messi has been involved in charitable efforts aimed at children, a commitment that stems in part from the medical difficulties he faced in his own childhood. Since 2004, he has contributed his time and finances to the [United Nations Children's Fund](/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF") (UNICEF), an organisation that has also collaborated with [FC Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").[[374]](#cite_note-Leo_Messi:_Goodwill_Ambassador-405)[[375]](#cite_note-406) Messi has served as a [UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador](/wiki/UNICEF_Goodwill_Ambassador "UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador") since 2010; he completed his first field mission for the organisation that year as he travelled to Haiti to bring awareness to the plight of the country's children following the [2010 Haiti earthquake](/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake "2010 Haiti earthquake"). He has since participated in UNICEF campaigns related to [HIV prevention](/wiki/Prevention_of_HIV/AIDS "Prevention of HIV/AIDS"), education, and the social inclusion of disabled children.[[376]](#cite_note-407) In November 2013, Messi and his one-year-old son Thiago were part of a publicity campaign to raise awareness of mortality rates among disadvantaged children.[[377]](#cite_note-408)

In 2007, Messi launched the Leo Messi Foundation, which supports access to health care, education, and sport for children.[[378]](#cite_note-409) It was established following Messi's visit to a hospital in Boston for terminally ill children, an experience that resonated with him to the point that he decided to reinvest part of his earnings into society.[[379]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013576–577-410) Through his foundation, Messi has awarded research grants, financed medical training, and invested in the development of medical centres and projects in Argentina, Spain, and elsewhere in the world.[[379]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013576–577-410)[[380]](#cite_note-411) In addition to receiving funds from Messi's own fundraising activities, the foundation receives financial support from various companies which have endorsement agreements with Messi, with Adidas as the main sponsor.[[381]]

Main article: [Staten Island Technical High School](/wiki/Staten_Island_Technical_High_School "Staten Island Technical High School")

Staten Island Technical High School began in 1982 as an annex of Ralph R. McKee Vocational-Technical High School, located in the [New Dorp](/wiki/New_Dorp,_Staten_Island "New Dorp, Staten Island") neighborhood of Staten Island, after [New Dorp High School](/wiki/New_Dorp_High_School "New Dorp High School"), which had occupied the building since it was built in the 1930s, moved to its current location on New Dorp Lane. The technical courses were taught in the annex, while the vocational courses stayed in St. George. Through the advocacy of parents, staff, and students, Staten Island Tech was made an independent high school by the New York City Board of Education in May 1988. Nicholas M. Bilotti, who had been serving as director of the annex, was appointed principal of the new high school.

**Lyndon Baines Johnson** (August 27, 1908 – January 22, 1973), also known as **LBJ**, was the 36th [president of the United States](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") from 1963 to 1969. Johnson was [vice president](/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States") under [John F. Kennedy](/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") from 1961 until [Kennedy's assassination](/wiki/Kennedy%27s_assassination "Kennedy's assassination") in 1963, when he assumed the presidency. Before becoming vice president, he served in both houses of the [U.S. Congress](/wiki/U.S._Congress "U.S. Congress"), representing Texas as a member of the [Democratic Party](/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)").

Born in [Stonewall, Texas](/wiki/Stonewall,_Texas "Stonewall, Texas"), Johnson worked as a teacher and a congressional aide before winning election to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1937. In 1948, he was controversially declared the winner in the Democratic primary for the [U.S. Senate election](/wiki/1948_United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas "1948 United States Senate election in Texas") in Texas before winning the general election.[[1]](#cite_note-2) He became [Senate majority whip](/wiki/Senate_majority_whip "Senate majority whip") in 1951, Senate Democratic leader in 1953 and majority leader in 1954. Senator Kennedy bested Johnson and his other rivals for the [1960](/wiki/1960_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "1960 Democratic Party presidential primaries") Democratic presidential nomination before surprising many by offering to make Johnson his vice presidential running mate. The Kennedy–Johnson ticket won [the general election](/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_election "1960 United States presidential election"). After the Revolution, the [Republicans](/wiki/Republicanism "Republicanism") favoured [Neoclassicism](/wiki/Neoclassicism "Neoclassicism") although it was introduced in France before the revolution with such buildings as the [Parisian Pantheon](/wiki/Panth%C3%A9on "Panthéon") or the [Capitole de Toulouse](/wiki/Capitole_de_Toulouse "Capitole de Toulouse"). Built during the French First Empire, the [Arc de Triomphe](/wiki/Arc_de_Triomphe "Arc de Triomphe") and [Sainte Marie-Madeleine](/wiki/%C3%89glise_de_la_Madeleine "Église de la Madeleine") represent the best example of [Empire style](/wiki/Empire_style "Empire style") architecture.[[319]](#cite_note-331) Under [Napoleon III](/wiki/Napoleon_III "Napoleon III"), a wave of urbanism and architecture was given birth; extravagant buildings such as the neo-Baroque [Palais Garnier](/wiki/Palais_Garnier "Palais Garnier") were built. The urban planning of the time was very organised and rigorous; most notably, [Haussmann's renovation of Paris](/wiki/Haussmann%27s_renovation_of_Paris "Haussmann's renovation of Paris"). The architecture associated with this era is named [Second Empire](/wiki/Second_Empire_(architecture) "Second Empire (architecture)") in English, the term being taken from the [Second French Empire](/wiki/Second_French_Empire "Second French Empire"). At this time there was a strong Gothic resurgence across Europe and in France; the associated architect was [Eugène Viollet-le-Duc](/wiki/Eug%C3%A8ne_Viollet-le-Duc "Eugène Viollet-le-Duc"). In the late 19th century, [Gustave Eiffel](/wiki/Gustave_Eiffel "Gustave Eiffel") designed many bridges, such as the [Garabit viaduct](/wiki/Garabit_viaduct "Garabit viaduct"), and remains one of the most influential bridge designers of his time, although he is best remembered for the [Eiffel Tower](/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Monthly_Climate_Normals_%281991-2020%29_-_Juneau_Area%2C_AK%28ThreadEx%29.svg/250px-Monthly_Climate_Normals_%281991-2020%29_-_Juneau_Area%2C_AK%28ThreadEx%29.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Monthly_Climate_Normals_(1991-2020)_-_Juneau_Area,_AK(ThreadEx).svg)

Climate chart for Juneau

The Juneau area is in a transition zone between a [humid continental climate](/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") ([Köppen](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *Dfb*), a [subarctic climate](/wiki/Subarctic_climate "Subarctic climate") ([Köppen](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *Dfc*), and an [oceanic climate](/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") (Köppen *Cfb/Cfc*), depending on the isotherm used. The city's climate is heavily influenced by the proximity of the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean"), specifically the warm [Alaska Current](/wiki/Alaska_Current "Alaska Current"), and the [Coast Mountains](/wiki/Coast_Mountains "Coast Mountains") that form a natural [orographic barrier](/wiki/Orographic_lift "Orographic lift") for incoming air. As a result, the weather is mild and moist, which, as in other parts of the [Alaska Panhandle](/wiki/Alaska_Panhandle "Alaska Panhandle"), allows the growth of [temperate rainforests](/wiki/Temperate_rainforest "Temperate rainforest").[[36]](#cite_note-:1-36) Like other cities in southeast Alaska, Juneau does not have [permafrost](/wiki/Permafrost "Permafrost").[[37]](#cite_note-37) As of 2023, Juneau falls within [USDA](/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Agriculture "United States Department of Agriculture") [Hardiness Zones](/wiki/Hardiness_zone "Hardiness zone") 6B and 7A.[[38]](#cite_note-38)

There are two prevalent types of wind in Juneau. Particularly in winter, the [Aleutian Low](/wiki/Aleutian_Low "Aleutian Low") draws warm and moist air from the south, bringing ample snow- or rainfall, and even in summer, winds will tend to blow onshore.
